prompt:
Solve the running-time recurrence below.

```formula
T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n
where
T: the running time on input size n
n: the input size
In words: Four half-size calls are followed by linear outside work.
```

options.explanation:
This is the two-child merge-sort recurrence. Four children instead give a quadratic leaf count.

```formula
T_other(n) = 2T_other(n/2) + n
L(n) = n^{log_2(4)} = n^2
where
L: the four-child tree’s leaf count
T_other: the cost of that different two-child recurrence
log_2: the base-2 logarithm; log_2(x) is the power you raise 2 to in order to get x
n: the input size
In words: This is the two-child merge-sort recurrence. Four children instead give a quadratic leaf count.
```
This assumes matching root and leaf growth. Here linear outside work is polynomially smaller than quadratic leaves, so no extra logarithm is added.
Root domination requires outside work polynomially larger than leaf growth. The stated outside work is smaller instead.

Correct. Four half-size calls give critical exponent two, while linear outside work is smaller by a full power. Leaves dominate.

```formula
log_2(4) = 2
f(n) = n
T(n) = Θ(n^2)
where
T: the running time on input size n
f: the work outside the recursive calls
log_2: the base-2 logarithm; log_2(x) is the power you raise 2 to in order to get x
n: the input size
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constants
In words: Four half-size calls give critical exponent two, while linear outside work is smaller by a full power. Leaves dominate.
```

```formula

T(n) = Θ(n^c) = Θ(n^2)
N_k = 4^k
s_k = n/2^k
W_k = N_k s_k = n 2^k
where

log_2: the base-2 logarithm; log_2(x) is the power you raise 2 to in order to get x
a: the number of recursive calls per call
b: the shrink factor; each call gets n / b
f(n): the work outside the recursive calls
n: the input size
c: the critical exponent log_b(a); n^c is the number of leaves
log_2(4): the base-2 logarithm of 4, which is 2
ε: epsilon, the margin by which f is polynomially smaller (here 1)
O: Big-O, at most a constant times
Θ: Big-Theta, exactly this rate up to constants
N_k: the number of nodes on level k
W_k: the level’s total outside work
k: the nonnegative level index
s_k: the item count per node
In words: the outside work n is a whole power of n smaller than the n^2 leaves, so case 1 applies and the leaves set the cost.
```

The number of nodes quadruples while each child halves its size. Level totals therefore double, so the quadratic leaf count dominates, as the card records.

prompt: The Toom-3 multiplication algorithm splits each n-digit number into **three** parts and replaces the 9 part-products with **5** multiplications of one-third the digit count, plus linear work. What is its running time?

options.explanation:
This is schoolbook growth, obtained by using all nine third-size products.

```formula
T(n) = 9T(n/3) + n
n^{log_3(9)} = n^2
where
T: the running time of this alternative candidate recurrence on n-digit inputs
log_3: the base-three logarithm: the exponent producing its positive argument when three is raised to it
n: the number of digits
In words: This is schoolbook growth, obtained by using all nine third-size products.
```

This is Karatsuba-like growth with three half-size products. Toom-3 has a different branching and split factor.

```formula
T(n) = 3T(n/2) + n
log_2(3) ≈ 1.585
where
T: the running time of this alternative candidate recurrence on n-digit inputs
log_2: the base-2 logarithm
n: the number of digits
≈: approximately equal to
In words: This is Karatsuba-like growth with three half-size products. Toom-3 has a different branching and split factor.
```

A critical exponent of one would require only three third-size products. Five products make the exponent larger than one.

```formula
log_3(3) = 1 < log_3(5)
where
log_3: the base-three logarithm: the exponent producing its positive argument when three is raised to it
<, >, ≤, ≥: less than, greater than, at most, at least
In words: A critical exponent of one would require only three third-size products. Five products make the exponent larger than one.
```

Correct. Five third-size calls plus linear outside work fall into the leaf-dominated case.

```formula
log_3(5) ≈ 1.465

where

log_3: the base-three logarithm: the exponent producing its positive argument when three is raised to it
n: the number of digits

```

```formula
f(n) = n = O(n^{c − ε})
T(n) = Θ(n^{log_3(5)})
log_3(9) = 2
```
